newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Aviation fuel shortages ground flights in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Aviation fuel shortages ground flights in Nigeria.

text.p: A shortage of aviation fuel has paralysed flight operations between the Nigerian capital Abuja and the commercial city of Lagos, travellers and witnesses said on Tuesday.
They said flights between both cities, the busiest and most commercially-viable route for domestic airlines, had been cancelled.
"The airlines said they have cancelled all flights between Abuja and Lagos today," one journalist at the Abuja airport told Reuters by telephone from there.
"The situation here is hectic as many people who came here for the 1997 budget breakdown are stranded. Most of us have decided to return to Lagos by road," he added.

Finance minister Anthony Ani held a news conference in Abuja on Monday to give a breakdown of the 1997 budget -- called the common man's budget -- which military ruler General Sani Abacha announced at the weekend.
Some officials in Lagos said since last week, their airlines had resorted to getting supplies of aviation fuel from tanker drivers who have cashed in on the situation to push up prices.
"We understand there is shortage of aviation fuel because the NNPC (Nigerian National Petroleum Corp) has not lifted fuel since last week," said one airline official who declined to be named.

Ports sources say state-run Nigerian Ports Authority since last week has not allowed NNPC's fuel-loaded vessels from southeastern Port-Harcourt to berth in Lagos because it is owed four billion naira.

Fuel shortages are common in oil-rich Nigeria where poor management and lack of funds to buy spare parts for repairs had reduced production from its four refineries to about a third of their combined total capacity of 445,000 barrels per day.
The semi-official Daily Times newspaper quoted Bashir Dalhatu NNPC managing director as saying that efforts were being made to resolve the matter with the ports authorities.
